statement: Let $mS$ be an irreducible singular fibre in the setting of 4.2. Suppose its normalization $T$ is smooth and $d\nu:T_T\to\nu^*T_X$ has rank two away from finitely many points. Let $\ell$ be the length of its maximal-minor scheme. Then \[ e(T)=K_T^2-\ell. \] The alternatives for $T$ are a rational surface with $e(T)=6-\ell/2$ and $0\leq\ell\leq6$, a minimal ruled surface over an elliptic curve with $\ell=0$, or a Hopf surface with $\ell=0$. In either of the last two alternatives $e(S)=0$. The reduced conductor and singular locus are disjoint unions of smooth elliptic curves, and their normalization maps are finite and unramified.

For every integer $n\geq1$, the reduced hypersurface germ $x^2-zy^n=0$ cannot occur in a fibre of a proper holomorphic degeneration of complex two-tori with smooth total threefold, even with any positive common multiplicity on that germ. In particular the Whitney umbrella ($n=2$) is excluded. No hypothesis on $b_2$ is needed.

For all $a\geq2$ and $n\geq1$, the germ $x^a-zy^n=0$ is excluded in the setting of P4.16. Its affine nearby fibre has $\pi_1=0$ and compact second-homology intersection lattice $A_{a-1}(-n)$. This includes the order-three cyclic-ramification germ $x^3-zy^3$ and examples with singular normalization.

For $a\geq2$ and $b,c\geq1$, the reduced germ $x^a-y^bz^c=0$ cannot occur with a common positive multiplicity in a torus degeneration with smooth total threefold. Its affine nearby fibre contains a spherical class of nonzero square. In particular this excludes $x^2-z^3y^4$, whose smooth normalization has a divisorial differential rank drop.

The germ $y(x^2-zy^2)=0$ has ramified conductor, of multiplicity two on each normalization component, but its affine nearby fibre is $\mathbb C^*\times\mathbb C$. Ramification alone therefore does not give the spherical intersection obstruction of P4.16--P4.18. This is a local statement, not a compact counterexample to 4.2.

statement: The sheaf $E$ is locally free of rank two and is the pullback of the translation Lie bundle $V$ on $\widehat B$. There is an exact sequence \begin{equation}\label{eq:P5tangent} 0\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow T_X\longrightarrow J\longrightarrow0. \end{equation}

For every admissible twist of the $(3,4)$ construction, \[ \operatorname{Aut}(X_c)=\mathbb C/\mathbb Z\simeq\mathbb C^*. \] The parameter $a\bmod\mathbb Z$ acts by translation by $a\widehat\delta$.
For fixed admissible twist data, $X_c\simeq X_{c'}$ precisely when $c-c'\in2\mathbb Z$. This fixes the integral period of $c$; the construction still permits an additive choice of $\beta^{\rm part}$.

For every admissible member, its vertical translation bundle on $\widehat B$ and its first coherent direct image are \[ E_0=F^\vee=\mathcal O\oplus L^{-1}\oplus L^{-2},\qquad G=R^1h_*\mathcal O_M=\mathcal O\oplus L^{-1}\oplus L^{-2}. \] Moreover $R^qh_*\mathcal O_M=\bigwedge^qG$ for $0\le q\le3$, $K_M=h^*L^{-6}$, and \[ (h^0(\mathcal O_M),\ldots,h^4(\mathcal O_M))=(1,1,0,0,0). \]

For every admissible fourfold, \[ (h^0(T_M),h^1(T_M),h^2(T_M),h^3(T_M),h^4(T_M)) =(1,1,1,2,0). \] The complex parameter family has a nonzero Kodaira--Spencer map at every member and supplies a smooth one-dimensional miniversal Kuranishi germ.

The fourfold has algebraic dimension one and \[ \Aut^0(M)=\mathbb C,\qquad \Aut(M)=\mathbb C\times\mathbb Z/2. \] In a fixed holomorphic splitting, two members of the full admissible complex parameter half-plane are biholomorphic exactly when their parameters are equal.

There is no such analytic extension across any finite boundary point of $\mathcal H$, or across infinity. The same conclusion holds after any finite ramified change of the local boundary coordinate. A holomorphic punctured-disc family whose fibres are all members of this fourfold family has an interior parameter limit. Let $N$ be an endomorphism of $\Z^6$ with $N^2=0$, rank three, and primitive image. There is a unimodular basis in which \[ I+N=\begin{pmatrix}I_3&I_3\\0&I_3\end{pmatrix}. \] Its centralizer in $\operatorname{GL}_6(\Z)$ consists exactly of $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}P&Q\\0&P\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, with $P\in\operatorname{GL}_3(\Z)$ and $Q\in\operatorname{Mat}_3(\Z)$.

A finite-order integral linear action on $\R^6$ admitting a free finite affine torus lift has characteristic polynomial among exactly thirty-eight cyclotomic products. Their linear orders are \[ 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12. \] Exactly nineteen of these polynomials admit a commuting complex structure on $\R^6$. These are a preliminary spectral list; no assertion about global gluings is inferred from the list.

Let $W$ be a compact almost complex eight-manifold whose outward-oriented boundary is the homotopy sphere $\Sigma$. In the presentation $\Theta_7=\Z/28$ fixed on the first page, \[ [\Sigma]= \frac{-c_1^4+4c_1^2c_2+3c_2^2-3\sigma(W)}{24} \pmod {28}. \] All characteristic products are evaluated on $[W,\partial W]$ using their unique relative rational lifts. A spin assumption on $W$ is unnecessary.

The equation $6a=b$ in $\Z/28$ has no solution for odd $b$. For $b=2r$, its solutions are exactly $a=5r$ and $a=5r+14$ modulo $28$. Thus the sixfold class alone leaves precisely these two possibilities for the original class; absent a value of $b$, this calculation excludes no original class.

For a proper holomorphic degeneration of complex two-tori with smooth total threefold and central fibre $mS$, where $S$ is irreducible and reduced, the group $\pi_1(S)$ has an abelian normal subgroup with cyclic quotient of order dividing $m$.

In the setting of Part~4.2, every irreducible singular support whose normalization is smooth and whose normalization morphism is bijective has nonnegative topological Euler number. Its Euler number is zero precisely when that normalization is a minimal ruled surface over an elliptic curve or a Hopf surface.

In the setting of Part~4.2, let an irreducible singular fibre support $S$ have smooth normalization $\nu:T\to S$ whose minimal model is ruled over a curve of genus $g\ge2$. Write $D$ for the conductor divisor on $T$ and $C=\operatorname{Sing}(S)_{\rm red}$. The inclusion $D_{\rm red}\to T$ induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, and the normalization pushout induces $\pi_1(S)\simeq\pi_1(C)$. Moreover, \[ e(C)\ge0,\qquad e(S)>0. \] The assertion includes conductor components on different ruling fibres that map onto the same curve in $C$.

In the setting of P4R.1, choose a positive small-loop monodromy $A$ on $\Lambda=H_1(T^4;\mathbb Z)$. For a suitable $\lambda\in\Lambda$, a positive meridian of the reduced support is represented by $\mu=\lambda t^m$ in $\Lambda\rtimes_A\langle t\rangle$. The natural small-tube comparison gives \[ \pi_1(S)\simeq (\Lambda\rtimes_A\langle t\rangle)/\langle\!\langle\mu\rangle\!\rangle, \qquad \pi_1(S)/\operatorname{im}\Lambda\simeq\mathbb Z/m, \qquad b_1(S)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}\ker(A-I). \] For the support in P4R.3, a singular-locus incidence graph that is a tree of rational normalization components gives $e(S)\ge3$.

In the setting of Part~4.2, an irreducible singular support whose normalization is smooth and has a Hopf surface as its minimal model has nonnegative Euler number. More precisely, for its reduced conductor image $C$ one has $e(C)\ge0$. If the normalization is obtained by $k$ point blowups and $v$ of the exceptional curves belong to the conductor, then \[ e(S_{\rm reg})=k-v,\qquad e(S)=k-v+e(C)\ge0. \]

Let $S$ be an irreducible singular support in Part~4.2, let $\nu:N\to S$ be its normalization, and let $\rho:T\to N\to S$ use the minimal resolution of $N$. There is an effective integral divisor $D$ on $T$ such that \[ \omega_T(D)\simeq\rho^*\omega_S, \qquad \operatorname{Supp}D =\rho^{-1}(\operatorname{Sing}S)_{\rm red}. \] In particular $K_T+D$ is torsion, by P4.12. The strict-transform conductor has its usual positive integral coefficients. Every connected exceptional configuration over a singular point of $N$ has strictly positive coefficients in $D$. Every such configuration meets the strict-transform conductor.

It meets exactly one pole component, transversely once, and that component has pole coefficient one. In the double-horizontal-section case, $E$ is disjoint from the horizontal section. Distinct such components are disjoint; each is a leaf of the reduced ruling fibre. These assertions retain the multiplicities of the ruling fibre and do not require the multiplicity of $E$ to be one.

Put \(B=\mathbf C[u,v]\), \(R'=B[x,y]/(xy-uv)\), and \(J=(x,u)\subset R'\). The module \(J\) is flat over \(B\). Its fibre at \((u,v)=(0,0)\) is the normalization module \[ J\otimes_B\mathbf C\cong \mathbf C[x]\oplus\mathbf C[y] \quad\text{over}\quad\mathbf C[x,y]/(xy). \] For an integral projective nodal genus-one curve \(C\) with normalization \(\nu:\mathbf P^1\to C\), the rank-one torsion-free degree-zero sheaf \(\nu_*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1}(-1)\) has no cohomology. Thus the local magnetic module has an exact realization inside a flat family of torsion-free nodal sheaves. This supplies a candidate coefficient object for index excision. The local lemma does not by itself compare the actual return symbol; P3K.6–7 below provide that comparison by a real bordism.

Let \(B=S^3\times S^1\), let \(K\subset S^3\) be the cusp circle, and set \(T=K\times S^1\). Give the trivial real normal two-plane bundle of \(T\) its oriented complex-line structure. Its K-theory Thom map and extension by zero give \[ i_!:K^0(T)\cong K^0_c(N_T)\longrightarrow K^0(B). \] In the rank/degree basis of \(K^0(T)=\mathbf Z^2\), this map kills the rank generator and maps the degree-one reduced line class to the primitive top generator of \(\widetilde K^0(B)=\mathbf Z\). Every integer is consequently realized by a K-class supported on the cusp torus and vanishing on its complement. The spin index on \(B\) reads exactly this integer.

The free twelve-label construction of P3F.15, when applied to a reduced \(Q\)-central divisor with no stabilizers at its generic points, has multiplicity twelve over \(q=Q^{12}\) on every image component. A normal space with all those multiplicities equal to twelve admits no proper bimeromorphic map over the \(q\)-disc to the actual reduced cusp model. Thus a common proper toric modification of these two outer extensions cannot be inferred from their punctured-family comparison.

The integral connecting class from the marked boundary \(T^3\) has square zero and pairs trivially with every extension of the page line. In particular an odd cap correction does not change the normal Euler square.

Let one positive gamma turn denote the actual parameter cover whose angular clutch is P3F.13. The orbit family of this cover is the product \(Y\times S^1_\theta\), with \(Y=S^5\), and its fixed trace is \[ T_F=\{(R_\theta(p),\theta):p\in F\}, \] where \(R_\theta\) is the gamma rotation on the cusp orbit product of P3F.9. Use its product trivialization preserving the Seifert gamma coordinate. In these coordinates \(R_\theta\) is pure gamma rotation, including the explicitly trivialized source-translation suspension. There is a compact properly embedded oriented four-manifold \(X\subset Z=Y\times D^2\), with boundary \(T_F\), assembled from the actual page \(V\) and a product compression trace. Its complement has a unique integral class \(x\) with meridian value one. On the outer boundary this class is the actual delta-circle Euler class. On the graph copy of \(V\), its restriction to the framed normal section is exactly \(c_1(M)\).

statement: The real trace gives a spin bordism carrying the Euler line from the actual covered conifold return to a normal sphere bundle. Its index is zero. The original return also has index zero, and its actual Hopf-lift gluing is the standard sphere.

The same actual return index vanishes by a second calculation: vertical sphere quantization, an explicit marked cap switch, and acyclicity of the elliptic Picard line. This calculation does not evaluate the page signature, its line square, or its first Pontryagin number.

For the rotating framing specified below, the one-gamma-turn return has Jin characteristic numbers \((k,\ell)=(-6,-24)\). After removing an extending constant-rotation loop, this framing descends through the sixfold parameter cover. With the descended framing the original positive return has \[ k=-1,\qquad \ell=-4. \] Every other tubular framing differs by the explicitly described changes \((k,\ell)\mapsto(k+n,\ell+4n)\) of P3F.11. The asserted individual values include the framing; their index is independent of that choice.

Let \(S\) be the minimal regular elliptic surface with section \(O\) whose affine equation is \[ y^2=x^3-3f(t)x+2g(t),\qquad f=(t^2+1)^2+t,\qquad g=(t^2+1)^3+\frac32t(t^2+1)+\frac38. \] Put \(G=(t^2+1,\sqrt3/2)\), \(R=8G\), \(M=\mathcal O_S(R-O)\), and \(Q=G\). Choose any one of the four nodal fibres as the simple zero of the linearization. At the ordinary fibre \(t=0\), perform the multiplicity-one logarithmic gluing whose integral circle clutch is \(\widehat\gamma\). The resulting construction of Engel's Remark 8.5 gives a proper holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds diffeomorphic to the standard \(S^6\), over a punctured scalar disc \(0<|\lambda|<c\). For the positive \(\lambda\)-loop, with the complex orientation and the Eells--Kuiper convention of P3F.22, the return satisfies \[ A=-3,\qquad \mu(\Sigma_\Phi)=-\frac3{28},\qquad [\Phi]=25\in\mathbf Z/28. \] In particular this is a generator. The positive finite parameter pullbacks of this same family realize every oriented class in \(\Theta_7\). For every nonzero such class the mapping torus is not diffeomorphic to \(S^1\times S^6\).

Fix logarithmic orders \(3K,4L\), with \(\gcd(3K,4L)=1\), and primitive logarithmic coefficients \(n_0,n_1\), so \(\gcd(n_0,3K)=\gcd(n_1,4L)=1\). For the sphere members impose \(a=4L n_0+3K n_1=\pm1\), with zero additional cusp collar. Use the period coordinate \(c\) and scalar \(u\) of the original family. The closed higher parameter is \[ w_h=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\pi i c}{KL}\right), \qquad u=\kappa w_h^{2KL},\qquad \kappa\ne0. \] In particular, the original expression \(w=\exp(-\pi i c)\) does not give one closed higher loop when \(KL>1\). The positive sixfold cover \(w_h=r^6\) gives the signed gamma turn \(a\gamma\). For the positive-gamma sphere marking \(a=1\), with the descended rotating framing of P3K.9, the Jin integers of the positive \(w_h\)-loop are \[ (k,\ell)=(-KL,-4KL). \] The integer return index is zero for either sphere sign. These statements identify both the parameter and the framing in the supplied higher-order formulas.

In the rank-one Mumford model above a smooth elliptic source fibre, every double curve of the central cycle is elliptic and fixed by the line circle. A smooth cyclic descent, with the actual faithful root character on the base, retains an elliptic fixed curve. The same conclusion holds after potential good reduction of the source and for any number of permuted double curves. Such a descended local piece cannot occur in a smooth circle action on \(S^6\).

In a retained nonzero-linearization \(I_n\) neighbourhood, the circle quotient is the mapping torus of the actual source translation. If its global oriented orbit space has \(H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)=0\), that translation is transitive on the \(I_n\) components. In particular this conclusion applies to the retained neighbourhoods of the semifree sphere members with the single standard fixed \(\mathbb P^1\).

Let \(S\) be one of the rational elliptic surfaces with \({\rm MW}(S)=\mathbb ZG\). Write the generic Picard point of \(M\) as \(aG\), and the translating section as \(bG\). For a literal Remark 8.5 line with \(M\otimes t_{bG}^*M^{-1}=\pi^*\mathcal O(k)\), \[ k=ab\,h(G). \] At a retained \(I_n\) on which the translation is transitive, the whole-fibre linearization forces the generic Picard section to meet the identity component. At that fibre every vertical correction in \(M\) is a whole-fibre divisor. In particular, for the transitive component markings in the rank-one table, \(n\mid a\).

Every smooth sphere member with the standard fixed sphere and normal circle weights \((-1,+1)\) has a semifree line-circle action. For a cyclic affine log cap at a nonzero-linearization site, written on a smooth root source as a linearized line quotient, its actual circle orbit is a mapping torus of a smooth source-surface quotient. The finite zero-gamma subgroup and its line character are retained in this comparison. If the global orbit has \(H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)=0\), the resulting monodromy is transitive on the components of its central fibre. The descended line has multidegree zero there, and a vertical change with the same generic Picard point is an integer multiple of the primitive whole-fibre divisor.

For the whole-fibre \(I_1\) cusp construction of P3F.9, together with the actual nonzero-linearization affine caps of P3K.15, the delta orbit has a global map to a closed Seifert three-manifold over the original base \(\mathbb P^1\). Its regular fibres are connected elliptic tori. Every sphere member has at most two nontrivial effective gamma multiplicities. For two such multiplicities, write the marked local pairs as \((m_1,n_1),(m_2,n_2)\), with each pair primitive, and let \(b\) be the remaining integral gamma clutch. The exact restriction is \[ m_1m_2b+m_2n_1+m_1n_2=\pm1. \tag{P3K.16.1} \] In particular \(\gcd(m_1,m_2)=1\). Order-one clutches and the finite zero-gamma subgroups are retained in the source and line data; this restriction does not remove them.

The negative- and positive-diagonal OS49 families have equal actual return index for every cap order \(m=3k\), \(k>0\), every signed primitive twist \(n=\pm1\), and every additional integral delta twist \(d\delta\). Their index is zero, their oriented return class is zero, and their actual mapping tori are products as in P3F.24. The comparison is an oriented bordism carrying the actual Euler line; it imposes no spin hypothesis on the comparison bordism. The endpoint index structures are the prescribed ones from the original families.

In the actual whole-fibre \(I_1\) orbit projection of P3K.16, every sphere member has primitive source-fibre multiplicities at every logarithmic cap. In particular no cap whose smooth source quotient has a genuinely multiple central fibre occurs in such a sphere member.

For the actual affine root-line caps of P3K.15 in the sphere orbit scope of P3K.16, the root fibre is reduced. A singular root fibre has no nontrivial finite zero-gamma kernel. At a smooth elliptic root fibre that kernel is an actual normal root change, and the invariant source coordinates and line frames cancel it exactly. Thus the cap has a primitive effective pair without an unrecorded source or line quotient. At an original multiplicative fibre \(I_N\), a sphere cap retains the following necessary restrictions on the original source data \(M=\mathcal O(aG-O+D)\), \(Q=bG\): \[ \gcd(N,b[G])=1, \qquad a[G]=0\quad\text{in }\mathbb Z/N. \tag{P3K.19.1} \] For the explicit generator markings in P3F.2 these are \(\gcd(N,b)=1\) and \(N\mid a\). These restrictions hold at logarithmically replaced multiplicative fibres as well as at retained ones.

For a semistable multiplicative source fibre \(I_N\), a whole-fibre zero of order \(e\) has period determinant \(Ne\) and central Mumford fibre Euler number \(2Ne\), for every periodic unimodular triangulation. At an \(I_s^*\) zero, \(s>0\), the smooth quadratic semistable Mumford root, followed by its actual monomial involution quotient and toric quotient resolutions, has Euler contribution at least \(4se\). Potentially good zero sites are excluded from sphere members by P3K.12. In this actual smooth-root toric construction, a sphere member therefore has exactly one whole-fibre zero: a simple \(I_1\) zero. For a rational rank-one source, writing its generic line point and translation as \(aG\) and \(bG\), respectively, the height denominator \(d=1/h(G)\) satisfies \(ab=d\) after choosing the contracting generator and the sign of \(G\).

In the established sphere orbit and root-line cap scope, a nonzero-linearization \(I_s^*\) source fibre can occur only with \(s=1\), a primitive quadratic cap, and \[ a\equiv0\pmod2, \qquad b\equiv2\pmod4. \tag{P3K.21.1} \] The two \(I_3^*\) rank-one source configurations are excluded. Combined with P3K.19–20 and the actual source table, the remaining generic source coefficients are the 26 pairs in the 16 profiles displayed below. This is a proved finite restriction on the generic source data; it does not declare all remaining affine cap tuples to be sphere tuples without their integral gluing calculation.

For the following ten source profiles, let \(G\) be the marked primitive Mordell--Weil generator, put \(d=1/h(G)\), and choose \(M=\mathcal O(dG-O)\), translation \(Q=G\), a simple whole-fibre zero at an \(I_1\), and one order-one logarithmic gluing with gamma coefficient \(+1\) at a smooth source fibre. Use the standard vertical-edge unimodular cusp fan. These are compact complex threefolds diffeomorphic to \(S^6\). Their positive scalar-parameter loops have the indicated Jin integer and oriented \(\Theta_7\) class. \begin{center}\small\begin{tabular}{c p{0.48\textwidth} c c c}\hline OS row & Source profile & d & Jin integer A & Class mod28 \\ \hline 45 & \(I_8+4I_1\), \(I_8+II+2I_1\) & 8 & \(-3\) & 25 \\ 47 & \(I_7+I_2+3I_1\), \(I_7+I_2+II+I_1\), \(I_7+III+2I_1\) & 14 & \(-6\) & 22 \\ 55 & \(I_5+I_4+3I_1\), \(I_5+I_4+II+I_1\) & 20 & \(-9\) & 19 \\ 56 & \(I_5+I_3+I_2+2I_1\), \(I_5+I_3+III+I_1\), \(I_5+IV+I_2+I_1\) & 30 & \(-14\) & 14 \\ \hline\end{tabular}\end{center} The compact page is the indicated rational elliptic surface itself. Its line is \(M\), with square \(-d\), and \((dG)\cdot O=(d-2)/2\). Every displayed mapping torus is therefore not diffeomorphic to \(S^1\times S^6\), by the same oriented mapping-torus detection used in P3K.10 and P3F.25. There is also a restriction on additional smooth-site caps for these primitive sources. After the actual finite-kernel cancellation of P3K.19, let their primitive cap data be \((m_i,n_i,\lambda_{ai},\lambda_{bi})\), with \(\gcd(m_i,n_i)=1\). The exact orbit Mayer--Vietoris computation below gives, whenever its first-homology gluing matrix is unimodular, \[ H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)=\bigoplus_i(\mathbb Z/m_i)^2. \tag{P3K.22.1} \] Consequently a sphere member with only such smooth-site modifications has \(m_i=1\) at every site. For order-one sites the total gamma coefficient \(\sum n_i=\pm1\) gives sphere topology, including arbitrary integral source and delta collar coefficients. Consider one of the actual sphere families constructed above with a semifree fixed curve \(F\simeq\mathbb P^1\), whose complex normal bundle is \(\mathcal O(-1)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)\). Perform the toric flop of this fixed edge in the periodic cusp model, retaining the actual parameter clutch and all exterior gluings. Write the original positive return's Jin index as \[ A=\frac{4k-\ell}{24}, \] The positive return of the flopped family has oriented class \[ -5A\pmod {28} \tag{K23.1} \] in the run's normalization of \(\Theta _7\). For the family of P3F.37, put $m=4l+3$, $l\ge0$, and retain its actual parameter $\lambda=r^m$. For each of the ten scalar-parameter families of P3K.22, retain its actual period group, cap gluing, physical delta circle, and positive scalar-parameter loop. For the actual index-one cusp with its three complex double curves, use positive complex normal meridians \(m_i\) and the relative dual basis \(m_j\cdot D_i=\delta_{ji}\). Every sphere family obtained from a rational elliptic source with Mordell--Weil group \(\mathbb Z\) in the uniformly expanding case of E26 Remark~8.5 has the following exact inverse-action comparison. The physical fan and line circle are retained. The same statement holds on each specified root-parameter cover; no additional shorter-loop descent is asserted.

In the two starred Mordell--Weil entries, the full marked forms are \[ \begin{aligned} E_7:\quad &y^2=x^3+3r x^2+t x+1,\qquad G=(0,1),\\ E_6+A_1:\quad &y^2=x^3+3r x^2+A t x+t^2,\qquad G=(0,t). \end{aligned} \] The explicit coordinate, finite-root, resolved-quotient and Cartier-line maps below retain all allowed coefficients. For every actual family and positive parameter loop of P3K.27 or P3K.30, retain its physical delta cocharacter and all exterior gluings, and use any allowed index-one periodic unimodular cusp fan \(T(v,w)\). Write \[ \delta_{\rm circle}=r v+s w,\qquad S=r^2-rs+s^2,\qquad \gcd(r,s)=1. \] Let \(k,\ell,A=(4k-\ell)/24\) be the initial vertical-edge integers in the actual Cox framing of those statements. Consider the actual source and root-cap data of P3F.36, P3F.38, P3F.41--43, P3F.46--47, and the primitive-source data of P3K.22. Fix one of the whole-fibre sphere source tuples of K20--21 and F36--51, its marked translating point \(Q=bG\), its generic line point \(aG\), a selected simple \(I_1\) zero, and its effective cap data.
